claude.sample_unit: participants (243 medical professionals, 276 pediatric patient family members)

links.outcome: Participants' ability to identify AI-generated versus human-authored patient education material
links.effect: Only 7.3% (25/344) of participants assigned to LLM groups identified the material as LLM-generated, versus 80.6% (141/175) of PEAR participants identifying human authorship; overall correct identification 32%.
links.quote: While 80.6% (141/175) of participants in the PEARs group accurately recognized published expert-authored content, merely 7.3% (25/344) in the AI-generated groups correctly identified the content as LLM-generated.

links.outcome: Effect of LLM linguistic simplification on ratings and readability indices of patient education materials
links.effect: Simplification reduced word count, difficult words, and sentence length, but overall scores did not improve versus expert-authored materials (MPs 72.98 vs 72.97; families 65.47 vs 64.18; Holm-adjusted P>.99).
links.quote: Although all 3 indices decreased, the scores on the overall scale and 4 dimensions did not increase.

links.outcome: Perceived quality and usefulness of LLM-simplified plain-language patient education versus expert-authored
links.effect: AI-SRs vs PEARs total scores not significantly different in either group (mean difference 0.01 for professionals, 1.29 for families; Holm-adjusted P>.99), though word count and difficult words decreased.
links.quote: Additional language simplification did not improve acceptance in this predominantly highly educated sample, and the strong tendency to attribute materials to human authors highlights the importance of source transparency.

unlisted_practices: Using LLM simplification prompts to generate patient education materials and assessing perceived acceptance

links.effect: AI-GRs vs PEARs total scores: professionals 76.17 vs 72.97 (Holm P=.53); families 68.77 vs 64.18 (Holm P=.15); AI-SRs vs PEARs adjusted P>.99.
links.quote: After Holm correction, none of the prespecified comparisons between either AI group and PEARs was statistically significant for the overall score or its 4 dimensions.

links.effect: Only 7.3% (25/344) in AI-generated groups correctly identified content as LLM-generated; 80.6% (141/175) recognized PEARs as expert-authored.
links.quote: While 80.6% (141/175) of participants in the PEARs group accurately recognized published expert-authored content, merely 7.3% (25/344) in the AI-generated groups correctly identified the content as LLM-generated.

links.effect: AI-SRs vs AI-GRs: words 128 vs 157, difficult words 52 vs 63, sentence length 9.33 vs 10.07, all Holm P<.001; total scores did not increase.
links.quote: Although all 3 indices decreased, the scores on the overall scale and 4 dimensions did not increase.

screen.practice: LLM simplification of patient education materials (reading-level constraint)
screen.reason: Randomized double-blind study testing large language model-generated vs AI-simplified educational responses evaluated by both healthcare professionals and patient families.
